analysis:
Examined three provider-swift memory/performance changes: KVPoolReclaimer.swift (head lines 100-133, 152-167, 192-218, 225-254), ProcessMemoryLedger.capacityShortfall (head 198-224), and WholeMacServiceBudget.isIdle(for:)/performIfIdle (patch hunk at 224-247). These are availability and memory-accounting changes. They do not touch the coordinator WebSocket contract, keys, attestation, App Attest authorization, or the encrypted cache crypto.

KVPoolReclaimer: the sweep now has an idle/pressure/closed window and re-checks isReclaimAllowed() on the actor before the blocking native callback. The rate limit is recorded only for a flush that ran; idleClearCache returns false when the Mac is no longer idle, so no reclaim is recorded. releaseRetained is a non-blocking request. Telemetry uses a lock-backed store with saturating arithmetic. Nothing here appears to weaken T-010 or T-029 (availability) or T-028 (residual GPU data). Clearing the cache more often may marginally help T-028. Available evidence shows no secret or plaintext exposure.

ProcessMemoryLedger.capacityShortfall: read-only under the ledger lock. It uses overflow-checked adds and saturates to .max. It computes max(cap-side, OS-side deficit), consistent with headroom(); it does not mutate state, grant charge, or bypass replaceCharge/recheckCharge. Lock order is unchanged: it calls readUsage under the ledger lock, as existing methods do. Unmaterialized bytes are computed as charged - materialized, which is safe as long as the ledger invariant materialized <= charged holds.

WholeMacServiceBudget.performIfIdle: runs the body under the budget lock, which blocks admission and unbounded-activity starts. The documented contract is that the body must not reenter the budget. The body's contents are not in the supplied evidence. If the sweep's idle clearCache callback (a blocking GPU sync) runs inside performIfIdle, it holds the admission lock for the duration of a GPU sync. That is a possible availability and lock-contention concern, the same class as the wedge the reclaimer was written to fix. The wiring (ProviderLoop, StandaloneServer, and the idleClearCache closure) is not in this batch. The next review pass should verify the following: the lock is not held across unbounded GPU work; no path calls the budget from the body; and lock ordering against the native Admission and ledger locks is acyclic.

No concrete security regression is established from the supplied code.
